mainTopic: מחוסר זמן in מעשר בהמה, defining טינוף, the silent Jewish seller and בכורה, and a blood mass expelled by a large animal
overview: This amud covers several topics. First, a ברייתא shows that according to רבי שמעון, an animal too young to be offered (מחוסר זמן) still enters the pen for מעשר בהמה, just as a בכור is holy before it can be offered. The גמרא asks why he compares it to בכור and not to ordinary קדשים. Each side has four similarities, so the גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון learns it from a גזירה שוה on the word ״העברה״. Next, the גמרא defines the משנה's טינוף: רבא calls it a murky discharge and שמואל calls it bubbles of blood. It must be shown to a 'חכם', which רב פפא explains means an expert shepherd. רב חסדא asks how long a fetus takes to form in an animal, and the attempted proof from זעירי is rejected, so his question remains unresolved. רב, שמואל and רבי יוחנן then argue about an animal bought from a Jew: is its offspring a definite בכור, a ספק, or definitely חולין? A ברייתא about אותו ואת בנו seems to refute רב and שמואל, but the גמרא distinguishes the cases. Finally, a new משנה rules that a blood mass expelled by a large animal must be buried, and the גמרא asks why, since רבי חייא teaches that it carries no טומאה. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא: a young animal enters the pen like a בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי שמעון rules that an animal too young to be offered (מחוסר זמן) still enters the pen for מעשר בהמה. He compares it to a בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: An animal whose time has not yet come enters the pen to be tithed. These animals are like a בכור. Just as a בכור becomes holy before its time and is offered after its time, so too an animal whose time has not come becomes holy before its time and is offered after its time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for רבי שמעון's view that even very young animals are included in the tithing of animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal under eight days old cannot yet be brought as a קרבן. Even so, a בכור is holy from the moment it is born and is simply offered later. רבי שמעון says the tenth animal in מעשר works the same way: it becomes holy now and is offered once it is old enough.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal 'lacking time', too young (under 8 days) to be offered
The animal pen where the tithing count takes place
To be tithed (counted for מעשר בהמה)
A firstborn male animal, holy from birth
Becomes holy before it is old enough to be offered

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the question that follows: why compare מעשר specifically to בכור and not to other קדשים?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says
in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
An animal whose time has not yet come enters the pen to be tithed,
and they are like a firstborn —
just as a firstborn is holy before its time
and is offered after its time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מְחוּסַּר זְמַן קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ
phrases.english: so too an animal lacking time is holy before its time
and is offered after its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier discussion of רבי שמעון's view on the previous section of the daf
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's position that a מחוסר זמן is included in מעשר בהמה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון, using a comparison to בכור

steps.title: Why learn from בכור and not from regular קדשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the comparison: why not learn מעשר from ordinary קדשים, which would point the other way?
steps.simpleTranslation: But instead of learning it from בכור, let him learn it from קדשים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's choice of comparison. Ordinary קדשים might suggest a young animal does not become holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the Sefaria explanation, regular sacrificial animals cannot be consecrated before they are old enough. If מעשר were compared to them, a מחוסר זמן would not enter the pen. So the choice of comparison decides the law.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary sacrificial animals consecrated by a person

phrases.english: But rather than deriving from a firstborn,
let him derive from sacrificial animals?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison used in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of מעשר to בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another possible model, קדשים, that would give the opposite result. Why prefer בכור?

steps.title: מעשר shares four features with בכור
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בכור is the better comparison, because מעשר and בכור share four features, remembered as גואל, מום, תמורה, אכילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to learn from בכור, since they share: redemption, blemish, substitution, and eating.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the comparison to בכור by listing four ways that מעשר and בכור are alike and different from other קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גואל: neither can be redeemed, even with a blemish. מום: a blemished animal still gets holiness. תמורה: an animal exchanged for them is not offered. אכילה: once blemished, they are eaten without redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: It is logical / it makes sense
A substitute animal exchanged for a holy one

steps.confusionAlert: These four words are a memory aid (סימן), not full sentences. Each word stands for a whole הלכה that בכור and מעשר share.

phrases.english: It is reasonable that he should derive from a firstborn,
since they share: redemption, blemish,
substitution, eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by showing more similarity to בכור
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe קדשים is an equally good model
steps.terutzMaskana: בכור is closer because of four shared הלכות

steps.title: On the contrary: מעשר shares four features with קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: מעשר is equally similar to קדשים in four other ways, remembered as זכר, קדוש, מתנות, פשוט.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, he should learn from קדשים, since they share: male, holy, gifts, and ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא counters the previous answer. It shows four ways that מעשר is like ordinary קדשים and unlike בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זכר: מעשר and קדשים include females, while בכור is only male. קדוש: both become holy through a person's action, while a בכור is holy from the womb. מתנות: neither is a gift to the כהן, while בכור is. פשוט: both are ordinary animals, not 'first-born'. Now the count is four against four.

keyTerms.meaning: Male (בכור is limited to males; the others are not)

phrases.english: On the contrary, he should derive from sacrificial animals,
since they share: male, consecrated,
gifts, ordinary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer by showing equal similarity to the other side
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בכור is the more logical model
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There are four similarities to קדשים as well, so logic alone cannot decide.

steps.title: רבי שמעון learns it from a גזירה שוה of ״העברה״
steps.stepSummary: Since logic is tied, the גמרא concludes that רבי שמעון learns the law from a גזירה שוה on the shared word ״העברה״ (passing) used for both בכור and מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי שמעון learns it from the shared word ״העברה״ ״העברה״.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the logical comparison and explains that רבי שמעון's source is a word-link in the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By בכור the תורה says ״והעברת״ (שמות יג:יב), and by מעשר it says ״כל אשר יעבר תחת השבט״ (ויקרא כז:לב). A גזירה שוה is a received tradition, so it holds even when logic is evenly balanced.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Passing', the word shared by the בכור and מעשר פסוקים
He learned it (by tradition / גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון includes a מחוסר זמן in מעשר because of a גזירה שוה ״העברה״ ״העברה״ from בכור, not because of logical similarity. The logical comparisons were four against four.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Shimon
learns 'passing' 'passing' (a verbal analogy).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the objection and moves to a textual source
steps.terutzResolutionType: Switching from logical comparison to a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון compared מעשר to בכור by logic
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון relies on the גזירה שוה of ״העברה״

steps.title: What is a טינוף?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns back to the משנה and asks what exactly a טינוף is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a טינוף like?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא asks for a definition of the משנה's word טינוף, setting up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that if an animal expels a טינוף, it counts as a first birth, so the next offspring is not a בכור. We need to know exactly what discharge qualifies.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? / How do we picture it?
A murky discharge from the womb

phrases.english: What is a murky discharge?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section on the משנה's term

steps.title: רבא: as the shepherds say
steps.stepSummary: רבא defines טינוף using a shepherds' saying: a murky discharge shows a fetus the animal held in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: As the shepherds say, 'A murky discharge — the animal held it in.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by quoting a saying of shepherds about what a murky discharge means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying means that a murky discharge comes from a fetus that formed inside the animal and broke down. So it counts as a real birth.

phrases.english: Rava said: As the shepherds say:
A murky discharge — the animal held (a fetus) in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A murky discharge, showing a fetus held in the womb

steps.title: שמואל: bubbles of blood
steps.stepSummary: שמואל gives a different definition: טינוף is bubbles of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: Bubbles of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל offers a second definition of טינוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא describes a murky fluid, while שמואל describes clumps or bubbles of blood. Each describes a different-looking sign of a fetus.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: Bubbles of blood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same question

steps.title: The discharge must be shown to a חכם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that the discharge must be shown to a חכם to decide whether it is a real טינוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one must show it to a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical rule: an expert must examine the discharge. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every discharge means there was a fetus. So the owner cannot decide alone, and an expert must judge.

phrases.english: And one must show it to a Sage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a practical requirement
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A possible טינוף must be examined by a חכם

steps.title: How would a Torah scholar know?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a Torah scholar would know how to identify animal discharges.
steps.simpleTranslation: A חכם — how would he know?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the rule: a Torah scholar is not an expert in animal births.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Identifying a טינוף is a matter of hands-on experience with animals, not Torah knowledge. So sending it to a 'Sage' seems strange.

phrases.english: A Sage — from where would he know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the word חכם in the previous rule
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement to show the discharge to a חכם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A scholar lacks the practical knowledge needed to identify animal discharges.

steps.title: רב פפא: an expert shepherd
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'חכם' here means a shepherd who is an expert.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: An expert shepherd.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא resolves the difficulty: the word 'חכם' here means a shepherd who is skilled in this area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חכם does not always mean a Torah scholar. It can mean any skilled expert. Here the expert is an experienced shepherd who knows what different discharges look like.
steps.whatToRemember: טינוף is a murky discharge (רבא) or bubbles of blood (שמואל). It must be examined by a 'חכם', which רב פפא explains is an expert shepherd.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: A knowledgeable shepherd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by redefining the word
steps.terutzMaskana: חכם here means an experienced shepherd

steps.title: A human fetus takes forty days to form
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא cites a known rule: a human fetus is considered formed after forty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The Sages said that a fetus in a woman takes forty days to form.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא states a known fact about humans. He is setting up a question about animals in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps discussed טינוף, a discharge showing that an animal carried a fetus. To know when a discharge counts as a real fetus, we need to know how long a fetus takes to form. The human rule of forty days is the starting point.

keyTerms.meaning: The formation of the fetus, the point when it counts as a formed baby

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
They said: the formation of a fetus in a woman
is forty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of טינוף by asking how early a fetus actually forms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A human fetus is formed at forty days.

steps.title: How long does a fetus take to form in an animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what the forming time is for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא asked: In an animal, how many days does it take?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks a real question: we know the number for humans, but what is it for animals?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Animals have different pregnancy lengths than humans, so the forty-day rule cannot simply be copied over. The answer matters for deciding when an animal's discharge counts as a real fetus that would exempt its next offspring from בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (an open question, not an attack)

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda asked:
In an animal, how many days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the human rule from step 12 and asks about animals.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How many days it takes a fetus to form in an animal.

steps.title: רב פפא suggests זעירי already answered this
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests to אביי that זעירי's rule, that there is no טינוף before thirty days, answers רב חסדא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Isn't this the same as זעירי's teaching? For זעירי said: There is no טינוף in less than thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a possible answer to רב חסדא's question, using a statement of זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא reads זעירי as saying a discharge cannot count as a fetus until thirty days after conception. If that reading is correct, an animal fetus forms in thirty days, and the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this the same as...? (suggesting an earlier source already answers it)
An אמורא whose teaching is being quoted

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Isn't this the teaching of Ze'eiri?
For Ze'eiri said:
There is no murky discharge in less than thirty days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 13.
steps.raayaObject: An animal fetus forms in thirty days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: זעירי: אין טינוף פחות משלשים יום.

steps.title: זעירי was talking about something else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. זעירי's thirty days refers to how long after a טינוף the animal will not accept a male, not to how long a fetus takes to form.
steps.simpleTranslation: That statement was said about accepting a male.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רב פפא's suggestion by reading זעירי's words differently. רב חסדא's question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, זעירי meant that after a טינוף the animal does not accept a male for thirty days. That number says nothing about when a fetus forms, so it cannot answer רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: To accept (a male), meaning to become receptive to mating

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read זעירי's thirty days as a pregnancy timeline. The גמרא concludes it refers to the period after a discharge when the animal will not mate, and the forming time for animals is left unresolved.

phrases.english: That was stated regarding accepting a male.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 14.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using זעירי's statement as an answer to רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: זעירי's thirty days is about when the animal will accept a male, not about when a fetus forms.

steps.title: What about an animal bought from a Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה dealt with buying an animal from a גוי. The גמרא asks what the law is when the animal is bought from a Jew and we do not know whether it already gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found the case of one who buys from a גוי. What about one who buys from a Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It moves from the משנה's case of a גוי seller to a Jewish seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוי seller has no reason to tell us about בכורה, so we have no information. A Jewish seller knows the laws of בכור. The question is whether his silence tells us anything about whether the animal already gave birth.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (the case in the משנה)
One who buys from a non-Jew
One who buys from a Jew

phrases.english: We have found the case of one who buys from a gentile;
what about one who buys from a Jew?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצִינוּ לוֹקֵחַ מִגּוֹי, לוֹקֵחַ מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, extending the משנה's case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The בכור status of the offspring of an animal bought from a Jew when we do not know if it gave birth before.

steps.title: רב: The offspring is a definite firstborn
steps.stepSummary: רב says the offspring is a definite בכור. If the animal had already given birth, the seller would have boasted about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is a definite בכור. If the animal had already given birth, the seller would surely have bragged about it to the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer and reads meaning into the seller's silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that already gave birth is worth more to a buyer, because its next offspring will not have to go to the כהן. A seller would mention that to raise the price. Since he said nothing, the animal must never have given birth, so its next offspring is a definite בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: That it already gave birth to a firstborn

phrases.english: Rav said: It is a definite firstborn,
for if it were so that it had already given birth,
he would certainly have boasted about it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The offspring is a definite בכור, because the seller would have boasted if the animal had already given birth.

steps.title: שמואל: The offspring is a doubtful firstborn
steps.stepSummary: שמואל says the offspring is a ספק בכור. The seller may have kept quiet because he assumed the buyer wanted the animal for slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: It is a doubtful בכור. The seller thought the buyer wanted it for slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the seller's silence proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the seller thought the animal was bought for meat, its birth history would not matter to the buyer, so he had no reason to boast. His silence therefore tells us nothing, and we are left with a doubt.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: It is a doubtful firstborn,
since the seller thought he wants it for slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes רב's reasoning from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The offspring is a ספק בכור, because the seller's silence can be explained by his thinking the animal was for slaughter.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: The offspring is definitely non-sacred
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the offspring is definitely חולין. If the animal had not yet given birth, the seller would have warned the buyer about the prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: They are definitely חולין. What is the reason? If the animal had not given birth, then since a prohibition is involved, the seller would surely have told him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a third view that is the opposite of רב's. He also reads meaning into the seller's silence, but in the other direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב assumed a seller speaks up to boast. רבי יוחנן assumes a Jewish seller speaks up to protect the buyer from an איסור, since a בכור cannot be used normally. Since the seller said nothing, the animal must already have given birth, so the next offspring is ordinary חולין.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on the silent Jewish seller. רב: he would have boasted, so it is a definite בכור. שמואל: he thought it was for slaughter, so it is a ספק. רבי יוחנן: he would have warned about the איסור, so it is definitely חולין.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: They are definitely non-sacred.
What is the reason?
If it were so that it had not given birth,
since there is a prohibition involved,
he would certainly have informed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view, opposite to רב's.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The offspring is definitely חולין, because the seller would have warned about the איסור if the animal had not yet given birth.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about אותו ואת בנו says that if the seller did not inform the buyer, the buyer may slaughter without worry. This seems to support רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רבי יוחנן, who says חולין: If the seller did not inform him, the buyer goes and slaughters and does not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that appears to agree with רבי יוחנן's idea that a seller's silence means there is no איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under אותו ואת בנו, one may not slaughter a mother and its child on the same day. The ברייתא lets the buyer slaughter if the seller said nothing about selling the mother or child that day, which treats silence as meaning "no problem." That matches רבי יוחנן's assumption.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא כְּוָותֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּאָמַר חוּלִּין:
phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said non-sacred:
If he did not inform him,
he goes and slaughters and does not refrain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבי יוחנן's view in step 19.
steps.raayaObject: A seller's silence means there is no איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about אותו ואת בנו: if he did not inform, the buyer slaughters without concern.

steps.title: Does this refute רב and שמואל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the ברייתא disproves רב and שמואל, who do not rely on the seller's silence the way רבי יוחנן does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב and שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא follows the support for רבי יוחנן to its result: it seems to knock out the other two opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If silence about an איסור lets the buyer go ahead, then here too silence should mean there is no בכור problem. רב (definite בכור) and שמואל (ספק) both refuse that conclusion, so they seem to contradict the ברייתא.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Rav and Shmuel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the support for רבי יוחנן into a challenge against רב and שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא treats a seller's silence as proof that there is no איסור, which contradicts רב and שמואל.

steps.title: In one case the seller must speak, in the other the buyer must ask
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. For אותו ואת בנו the duty to speak is on the seller, so his silence means something. For בכור the duty is on the buyer to ask, so the seller's silence proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the matter depends on the seller. Here, the matter depends on the buyer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב and שמואל by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With אותו ואת בנו, the seller is required to tell the buyer, so if he stays quiet we can trust that there is nothing to tell. With בכור, the buyer is expected to ask about the animal's history, so a quiet seller has not failed any duty and his silence teaches us nothing. The ברייתא therefore does not refute רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter depends on the seller

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא does not refute רב and שמואל. A seller's silence only proves something when the seller is the one obligated to speak. In בכור, it is the buyer's job to ask.

phrases.english: There, the matter depends on the seller;
here, the matter depends on the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21 by distinguishing the cases.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between cases (who carries the duty to speak)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A seller's silence always means there is no איסור, so רב and שמואל are refuted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Silence counts only where the seller must speak. In בכור the buyer must ask, so רב and שמואל stand.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The three-way dispute among רב, שמואל, and רבי יוחנן remains open.

steps.title: A large animal that expels a mass of blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב rules that a mass of congealed blood expelled by a large animal must be buried, and the animal is exempt from בכורה from then on.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: if a large animal expelled a mass of congealed blood, it must be buried, and the animal is exempt from the law of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new case. A large animal such as a cow expels a lump of congealed blood, and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב gives two rulings about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, the lump must be buried, because a male fetus might have been inside it, and that fetus would be a holy בכור. Second, this counts as the animal's first birth (פטר רחם). So any later offspring is not a בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: A large domestic animal, such as a cow or donkey
Expelled or discharged from the womb
A lump or mass of congealed blood
Exempt from the firstborn law, so later offspring are not a בכור

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya tries to explain how the same mass can be serious enough to need burial, yet not be treated as a real fetus for other laws.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
A large animal that expelled a mass of congealed blood,
that mass must be buried,
phrases.notes: There may have been a male בכור inside it.

phrases.english: and the animal is exempt from the firstborn law.
phrases.notes: Its later offspring will not be a בכור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the earlier discussion about the seller's silence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mass of congealed blood expelled by a large animal must be buried, and the animal is exempt from בכורה for future births.

steps.title: The blood mass does not transmit impurity
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches a ברייתא: the mass of congealed blood does not make anything טמא, whether by touching it or by carrying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חייא teaches: it does not transmit impurity, neither by touching nor by carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of רבי חייא that adds a new detail. The blood mass does not carry the טומאה of a dead animal (נבלה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dead fetus is normally treated like נבלה, which makes a person טמא through touching or carrying. רבי חייא says this mass does not do either. That suggests it is not treated as a real fetus for טומאה. This sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying, impurity passed by carrying even without touching

phrases.english: Gemara:
phrases.notes: Start of the גמרא on this משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya teaches:
It does not transmit impurity,
neither through contact nor through carrying.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא about the טומאה status of the blood mass described in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mass of congealed blood does not transmit טומאה through touching or carrying.

steps.title: If it is not impure, why bury it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: since the blood mass does not transmit טומאה at all, it seems not to be a real fetus. So why does the משנה require burying it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And since it does not transmit impurity, neither by touching nor by carrying, why must it be buried?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets רבי חייא's teaching against the משנה and points out a contradiction. The answer will come in the next part of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial is required for a possible holy בכור, which means the mass is being treated as a possible fetus. But רבי חייא says it carries no fetus טומאה, which suggests it is not a fetus. The two rulings seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And since, introducing a premise that leads to a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not saying the משנה is wrong. It asks how both rulings can be true together: burial treats the mass as a possible fetus, while 'no טומאה' treats it as not a fetus.

phrases.english: But since it does not transmit impurity
neither through contact nor through carrying,
why must it be buried?
phrases.notes: The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמֵאַחַר דְּאֵינָהּ מְטַמְּאָה לֹא בְּמַגָּע וְלֹא בְּמַשָּׂא אַמַּאי תִּקָּבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי חייא's teaching in step 24 to challenge the burial ruling of the משנה in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the blood mass must be buried (תִּקָּבֵר).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Having no טומאה through touching or carrying shows the mass is not treated as a fetus. If it is not a fetus, it cannot be a possible holy בכור, so there seems to be no reason to bury it.
